claims.statement: For uniform nonidentity Q in G2 and uniform z in GT, sampled as in target-profile.json (Q=[b]Q0 with b uniform in [1,r), z=e(P0,Q)^a with a uniform in [0,r)), the Pollard kangaroo algorithm in proof.md recovers a with probability at least 0.5 (hence at least 0.39), and returns P=[a]P0 with e(P,Q)=z, with total work at most 2^128.465013 target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing and verification, under the disclosed random-walk heuristic of proof.md Section 4. Peak memory is at most 2^91 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^127.465013 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is 0 bytes. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. This is an analytic argument, not a claim of practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check the Pollard kangaroo logic (tame walk from the top of the interval, wild walk from the secret, same jump function, distinguished points, recovery from the two cumulative jump sums) on small additive cyclic groups. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
